prefs.name: Non-ASCII to stdout without a guard
prefs.description: Windows console defaults to cp1252/cp949, so printing Korean, CJK or emoji raises UnicodeEncodeError and kills the process. GitHub Actions Windows runners default to cp1252.
prefs.question: Does this diff write non-ASCII text to stdout or stderr without an encoding guard, an encoding parameter, or a sys.stdout/stderr reconfigure?
prefs.guidance: A bare print() of a non-ASCII string literal is a violation. Passing encoding= to open(), calling sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding=...), routing through a helper that falls back to errors='replace', or keeping output pure ASCII are not. Docstrings and comments are not output and do not count.

prefs.name: Written files carry no BOM
prefs.description: A BOM makes Python read the first line as a broken identifier and stops @echo off from working in a Windows .bat, so every command echoes to the screen.
prefs.question: Does this diff write a .bat, .cmd, .py, or .ps1 file in a way that would emit a UTF-8 byte order mark?
prefs.guidance: Writing such a file with PowerShell Set-Content defaults to a BOM and is a violation. io.open or write_text with encoding='utf-8', or a UTF8Encoding($false) encoder, is not.

prefs.name: No tool calls through non-ASCII paths
prefs.description: When a path contains Korean characters cmd.exe cannot read it and the script fails silently.
prefs.question: Does this diff invoke a shell, batch file, or subprocess using a path that contains non-ASCII characters, without a short ASCII path alias?
prefs.guidance: A hardcoded non-ASCII path passed to cmd, subprocess, or a .bat argument is a violation. A short ASCII drive alias such as subst, a workdir passed as a separate argument, or an ASCII temp path is not.

prefs.name: No second abstraction for a concept the project already has
prefs.description: A second implementation of an existing concept doubles the later refactor burden. Keep one from the start.
prefs.question: Does this diff add a new module, class, or function that represents a concept that another existing module, class, or function in this project already represents?
prefs.guidance: A second implementation of an already represented concept, added alongside the existing one rather than in place of it, is a violation. Extending the existing abstraction, or adding something the project genuinely does not represent yet, is not.

prefs.name: Do not remove or rename a working symbol
prefs.description: The most common way a working implementation gets broken. Removing an exported symbol silently breaks everything that referenced it.
prefs.question: Does this diff remove, rename, or change the required signature of a symbol that other existing code in this project already references?
prefs.guidance: Deleting a function, class, constant, or entry point that another file still calls is a violation. Changing a parameter name, adding an optional parameter, or widening behaviour while keeping the old call working is not.

prefs.name: Do not add a broad except that returns None
prefs.description: except Exception: return None hides the cause. An environment problem then looks like a code problem and becomes impossible to diagnose.
prefs.question: Does this diff add a broad exception handler that returns None, or otherwise swallows an exception, on a code path that has already done real work, without logging the reason or restricting the caught exception to a specific type?
prefs.guidance: Adding `except Exception:` followed by a bare return, pass, or continue is a violation when it hides a failure that happened after real work was already done, because the cause is then lost and the work is wasted. Catching a specific exception type, logging the reason, or raising a typed error is not a violation. A try around a bare import of an optional dependency, used as a capability check that returns None when the package is absent, is not a violation either: that is the intended shape of an optional dependency probe, and the caller decides what None means.

prefs.name: Do not use id() as a cache key
prefs.description: CPython recycles memory addresses after GC. Measured on this machine: 35 of 50 tensor allocations reused an id. A collision returns another object's cached result.
prefs.question: Does this diff use id() of an object, or the object's memory address, as a dictionary or set lookup key for a value that is expected to stay valid?
prefs.guidance: Keying a cache on id(obj) or a raw address is a violation. CPython recycles addresses after garbage collection, so a different object can be allocated at the same address and a lookup can return that object's result; measured on this machine, 35 of 50 allocations reused an id. A scale or option in the key does not make it safe, because the colliding object can also use the same scale. Keying on an explicit id field, a content hash, a weak reference, or holding a strong reference to the object next to the cached value is not a violation.

prefs.name: Do not touch files the task did not ask for
prefs.description: Changing unrelated files makes reverting hard and drags in risk that has nothing to do with the original goal.
prefs.question: Does this diff modify files whose change is not required by the stated task, including changes the task did not ask for?
prefs.guidance: Touching a second component, a second node, test fixtures, or documentation that the task did not name is a violation when the task named a specific target. Reformatting an adjacent block only to satisfy the same task is not.

prefs.name: Optional dependencies must not degrade silently
prefs.description: When an optional dependency is missing the feature quietly turns itself off and the user sees no error at all.
prefs.question: Does this diff add a feature path that silently degrades to a no-op or a default when an optional dependency is missing, without any log line, warning, or user-visible signal?
prefs.guidance: An import that fails and returns None, with no message, is a violation. Logging a warning, emitting a ComfyUI warning node message, or checking the dependency once and reporting it is not.

prefs.name: Classify the public API impact
prefs.question: Classify the public API impact this change introduces.

labels.additive: Only backwards-compatible additions. Existing callers keep working unchanged.
labels.behavioral: Existing API stays callable but observable behaviour changes, such as different output values, ordering, timing, or masking.
labels.breaking: An existing export is removed or renamed, or now requires incompatible usage, or changes a node's registered input or output contract.

prefs.name: No new optional dependency import
prefs.description: Camera deliberately does not import mediapipe and a test asserts that. A new optional import can also turn a working import into a silent None.
prefs.question: Does this diff add an import of a package that is not already imported at module scope in this project, outside of tests?
prefs.guidance: A new third-party import in production code is a violation unless it is already a declared dependency used elsewhere. An import inside a test file is not.

prefs.name: Prompt and output assembly changes stay narrow
prefs.description: Camera builds conditioning and prompt strings. Restructuring them changes generation results for every existing workflow.
prefs.question: Does this diff restructure how the conditioning tensor, the prompt string, or the IMAGE output is assembled, rather than adding a new optional branch?
prefs.guidance: Reordering, re-bucketing, or re-assembling the existing prompt or output path is a violation. Adding a new node, or a new opt-in branch that leaves the default path unchanged, is not.

prefs.name: No new VAE decode in a per-frame path
prefs.description: A 128x128 latent decodes to 1024x1024 RGB. Doing that more than once per frame is a measured slowdown.
prefs.question: Does this diff add a new call that decodes a latent tensor with the VAE inside a path that runs once per frame or per panel, without a cache?
prefs.guidance: Adding vae.decode() on a per-frame path with no cache is a violation. Decoding once and caching, or decoding only on an explicit user-requested operation, is not.

prefs.name: No large tensor allocated on CPU then moved
prefs.description: Allocating on CPU and then calling .to(device) costs a full host allocation plus a transfer every call.
prefs.question: Does this diff create a tensor or array on the default device and then move it to another device, rather than creating it directly on the target device?
prefs.guidance: A construction followed by .to(device) or torch.tensor(...).cuda() is a violation. torch.ones(..., device=x) is not.

prefs.name: Intermediate VRAM is released on the failure path too
prefs.description: A cleanup call placed after the successful return does not run when the path raises, so the leak only appears under failure.
prefs.question: Does this diff add an intermediate tensor or decoded array in a function that can return early or raise, without releasing it on every exit path?
prefs.guidance: Allocating an intermediate whose cleanup sits after an early return or outside the exception path is a violation. Cleanup in a finally block, or a context manager, is not.
